'''The STEEM / HIVE / BLURT / MELEK / VKBT / CURE Matrix''' is the one page that puts all of it side by side. Two tables, and they are '''not the same kind of table'''. The distinction is the whole thing, and it is simpler than the jargon makes it sound:

'''A coin has a chain. A token is on one.'''

STEEM, HIVE, BLURT, MELEK and PRANA are '''coins''' — each one is the native unit of its own blockchain, secured by its own witnesses or miners, and if that chain stops the coin stops with it. VKBT and CURE are '''tokens''' — they are issued on somebody else's chain, through an engine layer, and they inherit that chain's security, blocks and fees rather than providing any. Neither is better; they are '''different objects'''. A coin is compared on its '''machinery'''. A token is compared on its '''specs'''. Putting a token in a column next to a coin produces a number that looks like an answer and means nothing.

Both tables on this page are '''generated from our own data files''', not typed by hand, so what you are reading is what the system actually holds.

== 1. The coins: STEEM, HIVE, BLURT, MELEK, PRANA ==

[[Figure:graphene-matrix|Five coins — each with its own chain — compared on the dimensions that actually differ.]]

Four of these five are the '''same codebase''' with different decisions bolted on. That is the point of the table — the interesting information is never "which is faster," it is '''which rule did each one change'''.

=== What each row of that table means ===
* '''Family''' — Graphene (the BitShares/Steem lineage: fixed operation set, 3-second blocks, no general-purpose virtual machine) versus EVM/PoW. PRANA is in the table because it is ours, not because it is a sibling.
* '''Consensus''' — all four Graphene chains are '''DPoS''': a fixed number of witnesses produce blocks, and stake votes them in and out. STEEM and HIVE run '''21''' (20 elected plus a timeshare slot). '''MELEK protects one slot at the consensus level for the AI witness in year one''', scoped to that one account and time-limited; after that it stands for election like any other.
* '''Throughput''' — high for social operations on anything Graphene, because a post or a vote is a cheap fixed op, not a contract call.
* '''Fee tier''' — '''feeless''', which is the single biggest architectural difference from an EVM chain. You do not pay gas; you spend '''Resource Credits''' generated by your staked POWER. Bandwidth is rationed by stake instead of priced by auction. PRANA, being EVM, is '''gas-metered''' and behaves nothing like this.
* '''Token standards''' — the native coin pair (STEEM/SBD, HIVE/HBD, MELEK/MBD) plus a '''side-chain''' for everything else. '''BLURT deliberately has no second stablecoin.'''
* '''Virtual machine''' — '''none on layer one''' for every Graphene chain here. '''This is why tokens exist at all.''' A coin's chain has a fixed op set and will not run your code, so Hive-Engine and MELEK-Engine are bolted on as the layer where arbitrary tokens can live. The engine is the reason the second table on this page needs to exist separately from the first. See [[Hive Engine and Smart Media Tokens]].
* '''Governance''' — on-chain, stake-weighted witness voting everywhere. HIVE adds the '''DHF''' proposal system.
* '''Launched''' — and this row carries the history. '''STEEM 2016''', the original. '''HIVE and BLURT both 2020''': HIVE forked away in March 2020 over the stake takeover, and BLURT forked separately with '''no curation rewards and no downvotes''' at all. '''MELEK 2026''', testnet, '''zero pre-mine'''.

=== The thing the table shows that prose hides ===
Read the ''note'' row across and you get a lineage rather than a product comparison: one chain, one acquisition, two forks that disagreed about what was broken, and a fourth built later by people who had watched all of it. BLURT's answer was "remove curation rewards." HIVE's answer was "remove the stake that took us over." MELEK's answer was "no pre-mine, and put the witness who teaches newcomers in the genesis set." Those are '''three different theories of what went wrong''', visible as three rows.

== 2. The tokens: the Specs ==

[[Figure:token-specs|VKBT and CURE against their actual peer group — other engine side tokens — on the dimensions that decide what a token is.]]

'''VKBT and CURE are tokens, not coins.''' They have no chain of their own; they are '''engine-issued''' on a host chain and inherit its blocks, its witnesses and its fee model. So their peer group is '''other engine tokens''' — POB, BBH, SWAP.BLURT and the rest of the tribe-token layer — and never the coins in the table above. Comparing CURE's market cap to STEEM's is the category error this page exists to prevent: it makes a four-figure number look like a failure instead of what it is, '''a deliberately tiny supply''' on a token that was never trying to be a chain.

We call this table '''the Specs''', the way you would read the specs off a part. Every dimension is one that actually determines what the token is:

* '''Total supply''' — the whole number in existence. '''VKBT: 2,315,564. CURE: 70,974.''' CURE's entire supply is about '''79 times Bitcoin's daily mint''' of 900 coins. That is the kind of scarcity that is hard to intuit until it is written next to something. '''Both numbers move''' — see §2.1.
* '''Holders''' — '''VKBT: 25,038. CURE: 14,965''' accounts holding something. '''And the next row is the one that keeps that honest.'''
* '''Holders of ≥1 whole token''' — '''VKBT: 5,375. CURE: 1,337.''' '''19,663 VKBT holders and 13,628 CURE holders hold less than a single token.''' That is '''airdrop dust''', and dust is not a community. Both numbers are published because publishing only the first would mislead. Going further up: '''VKBT''' has '''2,975''' holders of 10+ and '''1,074''' of 100+; '''CURE''' has '''430''' of 10+ and '''62''' of 100+.
* '''Share staked''' — '''VKBT 42% (973,568). CURE 71% (50,245).''' Staked tokens are not on the market, so '''the liquid float is far smaller than the supply''' — on CURE, roughly 20,700 units.
* '''VKF position''' — what the issuing account actually holds: '''970,224 VKBT (41.9%)''' and '''37,477 CURE (52.8%)'''.
* '''How acquired''' — and this is the row that matters most, because it is the row everyone assumes. '''Purchased at market.''' Not a founder allocation, not a pre-mine, not minted to ourselves. '''Bought, at the going price, like anyone else.'''
* '''How it is distributed''' — '''given away through curation programs'''. The position is not a stagnant bag; it is the float for a reward system being built. A large holding that is being '''distributed''' and a large holding that is being '''held for exit''' look identical in a market-cap chart and are '''opposites'''. See [[Curation Theory, Rewards, the Auction Window, and Honest Curation]].
* '''Emission''' — '''and this is a correction.''' An earlier revision of this page said "fixed, no ongoing mint." '''The chain says otherwise.''' VKBT carries a '''maxSupply of 500,000,000''' and CURE one of '''20,000,000''', the issuer can mint up to those ceilings, and '''supply has in fact grown between captures''' (VKBT from roughly 1.9M to 2.32M). What is true is that the emission is '''discretionary issuance by the issuer''', not '''algorithmic inflation''' — which is a real difference from the tribe tokens (POB, BBH) whose supply grows automatically with every post reward, and from a '''coin''' like BLURT, whose chain mints new units into a reward pool by consensus, because that is what a chain does. '''But "fixed" was wrong, and the ceiling is 215x the current supply.'''
* '''Where it trades''' — '''TribalDEX''', against HIVE / SWAP.HIVE.
* '''Market activity''' — stated plainly, and it is '''thin to the point of being notional'''. In the 24 hours before capture, '''VKBT traded 0.018 HIVE''' — about a tenth of a US cent — and '''CURE traded 0.000003 HIVE'''. The '''ask/bid spread''' is '''5x on VKBT''' and '''2,203x on CURE'''. '''A thin book is a fact about a token and belongs in its specs''', and a spread of two thousand times means there is no price, only two opinions a long way apart.
* '''Cap at 1:1 HIVE''' — a '''reference calculation''', not a valuation: what the supply would be worth if the token traded at parity with HIVE, at HIVE's own median feed price of '''$0.0560''' on the capture date. '''VKBT $129,672, CURE $3,975.''' It exists so the supply numbers have a scale, not to suggest a price — and note that '''this figure moves when HIVE moves''', which is most of why an earlier revision of this page carried much larger numbers.

=== The tiers ===
Not every token we hold is held for the same reason, and the matrix separates them:
* '''Premium positions — VKBT, CURE.''' Scarce supply, bought at market, being distributed through curation. '''Not for sale as operating fuel.'''
* '''Operating fuel — SWAP.BLURT.''' 300,000+ held, sold gradually and top-order-only so the book is not broken. A different tier entirely — and note what it is: a '''coin''' (BLURT) '''wrapped''' into token form so it can trade on an engine. The wrapper is a token; the thing inside still has its own chain. See [[Wrapped Tokens]].
* '''Tradeable — POB, BBH and similar.''' Earned by posting and curating, sold when HIVE is needed.

'''The names are not random, and the chain is the authority on them.''' Both are registered in the token's own Hive-Engine record, so there is nothing to infer. '''VKBT is the "Van Kush Beauty Token"''' — "A Token for Rewarding Beauty, and Providing Liquid to the Beauty Economy." '''CURE is the "Curator Rewards Token"''' — "A Token to Reward Curators and Token Holders on HIVE Blog. The more You Hold, the more You get back for Your Curation." ('''An earlier revision of this page guessed "Van Kush Bot Token" for VKBT. It was wrong''' — the registered name was there to be read.) They were built with intention, as part of a system that is still being built, and the matrix is how you check that claim against numbers instead of taking our word for it.

=== 2.1 Two earlier holder counts were published. Both were wrong, and the reason is worth more than the numbers ===
This library previously carried '''two different holder counts''' for these tokens, on two different pages, neither matching the other:

* an older matrix page, [[The Matrix Supply Holders and Market Cap|The Matrix: Supply, Holders, and Market Cap]], said '''VKBT 10,894''' and '''CURE 10,526''' holders;
* this page, in its first revision, said '''VKBT 986''' and '''CURE 999'''.

'''Neither was a real count.''' Both were '''artefacts of how the chain was being read''', and they were '''read with the same broken tool''' at two different settings:

* '''The ~986 / ~999 pair''' came from a '''single query at Hive-Engine's 1,000-row page cap'''. The API will not return more than 1,000 balance rows in one request; after filtering out the empty ones you land just under a thousand. '''The number was a page size wearing a holder count's clothes''' — which is why both tokens, with wildly different supplies, returned almost exactly the same figure. '''That coincidence was the tell, and it was missed.'''
* '''The ~10,894 / ~10,526 pair''' came from a '''paged read that walked by offset''' and stopped where '''Hive-Engine refuses any offset above 10,000''' — it returns `{"code":400,"message":"Invalid request"}` outright. The client caught that error and '''returned the short list without saying anything'''. So the count stopped a little past ten thousand '''because the server stopped answering''', not because the holders ran out.

'''The true figures, read by walking an `_id` cursor instead of an offset''' (which has no ceiling), and verified against two independent passes:

* '''VKBT''' — '''26,066''' accounts have ever held it; '''25,038''' hold something now; '''5,375''' hold a whole token or more.
* '''CURE''' — '''15,692''' have ever held it; '''14,965''' hold something now; '''1,337''' hold a whole token or more.

'''So the real holder base is far LARGER than either published figure''' — by 2.3x against the offset-capped count and by 25x against the page-capped one. '''And it is also far dustier than the raw number suggests''', which is why the ≥1-token row above exists.

'''The lesson, which is the point of recording this at all:''' '''a number can be sourced and still be an artefact.''' Both wrong figures came from real queries against the real chain. What made them wrong was the '''reading method''', and the failure mode was '''silence''' — a client that truncates without complaining will hand you a confident, precise, wrong answer every time. The fix was to page by cursor and to make an incomplete read '''report itself''' rather than return quietly; a figure that looks suspiciously round, or suspiciously close to a page size, now gets re-derived instead of cited.

=== Where the numbers come from ===
Every cell is a '''live Hive-Engine read''' captured on '''2026-10-04''' and rendered by `integrations/token-specs.mjs`; `integrations/token-specs-refresh.mjs` re-derives the whole block from the chain, so a stale number is a decision not to run it rather than an accident. '''An unsourced cell renders as a dash, never as a guess''' — if you see `—` in the table, it means we do not have that number, not that it is zero. '''And the refresher refuses to print anything from an incomplete read''', for the reason in §2.1.

== 3. How to read any matrix like this ==
* '''Ask first whether it is a coin or a token.''' Does it have a chain, or is it on one? Almost every misleading comparison in crypto starts by mixing the two, and no amount of correct arithmetic afterwards fixes it.
* '''Check the peer group.''' Most misleading comparisons are not wrong about a number; they are wrong about which things belong in the same table.
* '''Ask how the big holder got there.''' Purchased, mined, earned and allocated-to-self are four different facts that a percentage hides.
* '''Ask where the supply is going.''' Distribution and accumulation look the same on a holdings chart.
* '''Read "fixed emission" as a promise that can be checked.''' Either the mint authority is gone or it is not.
* '''Treat a dash as information.''' A table that fills every cell is usually guessing somewhere.
